source.title: Training Deep Networks with Stochastic Gradient Normalized by Layerwise Adaptive Second Moments
source.authors: Boris Ginsburg; P. Castonguay; Oleksii Hrinchuk; Oleksii Kuchaiev; Vitaly Lavrukhin; R. Leary; Jason Li; Huyen Nguyen; Yang Zhang; Jonathan M. Cohen

record.tranche_reason: Compares optimizer and batch-size choices using held-out performance, but does not measure training–test gaps directly or test the original versions’ full procedures.
record.gate_note: Reports held-out benchmark results for optimizer and batch-size comparisons. These bear on V4 and V5, but the paper does not report the corresponding training errors. Its generalization statements about NovoGrad are recorded only where a stated held-out result supports them.
record.test_reason: The study directly compares held-out performance across adaptive optimizers and momentum SGD, and across batch sizes at fixed epoch budgets. These test V4 and V5 without requiring numerical training–test gaps. Speech recognition extends the tested workloads.
record.authors_conclusion: The paraphrase is accurate: the authors conclude NovoGrad matches or exceeds the tested alternatives, is robust to initial learning rate and initialization, and works well at large batches. They also claim half Adam's memory footprint and state that NovoGrad and all models are open sourced. These are their conclusions; large-batch results still include accuracy losses.
record.recipe_differences: Introduces NovoGrad, an adaptive optimizer with layer-wise gradient normalization and decoupled weight decay; compares task-specific recipes and settings, rather than reproducing the original optimizer or batch-size studies.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported large-batch outcomes vary by batch size; for NovoGrad, increasing learning rate and weight decay improves ImageNet results, and 500-step warmup improves top-1 accuracy to 75.99%. On speech recognition, batch 32K has higher WER, which the authors attribute to fewer weight updates per epoch.

fits_no_version.finding: NovoGrad exceeds Adam and AdamW on translation BLEU, with different dropout settings.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Adaptive optimizer recipes differ in translation performance; this does not establish an adaptive-versus-SGD penalty.

fits_no_version.finding: NovoGrad has lower word-level perplexity than Adam/AdamW and a stated smaller training–validation gap than Adam.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Generalization can differ between adaptive optimizers on word-level language modeling.

record.problems: No training error is given for the benchmark comparisons, so most results cannot quantify a training–test gap. No uncertainty estimates are reported. Optimizers use different hyperparameters, schedules, and in some cases dropout; the paper reports extensive hyperparameter search for AdamW on ImageNet.
record.rows_left_out: None. ImageNet Table 1 rows at 200 and 300 epochs were omitted because they are additional epoch conditions for the optimizer comparison and the 100-epoch rows capture the primary comparison; Table 2 SGD comparator rows were omitted because the table compares prior large-batch methods rather than the NovoGrad batch sweep.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting versus natural-label held-out accuracy.
Width beyond interpolation and its effect on test error.
Convolutional versus fully connected architectures and local connectivity.
The learning-rate-and-schedule-only tuning restriction; equal or better training performance; SGD comparisons on translation and word-level language modeling; switching Adam to SGD.
Large-batch language modeling, longer-training remedies, and controlled isolation of individual recipe changes. Speech recognition is an additional workload.
Controlled dropout addition or removal; differing translation dropout settings do not isolate dropout's effect.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and ranking generalization gaps.
Removing memorized examples versus random examples.

missing.what: Separate ImageNet batch-32K result with 500-step warmup: top-1 accuracy 75.99%, versus 75.78% without warmup.
missing.locator: Section 4.2 and Table 2, NovoGrad warmup row

missing.what: Initial batch-32K recipe using linear learning-rate scaling and warmup achieves 75.09/92.27 top-1/top-5, compared with 75.78/92.54 after learning-rate and weight-decay changes. This records recipe dependence within the same batch size.

record.verdict_notes: No original-source exclusion applies. Table 5's displaced other-split columns caused errors in R17 and R19. Training–test gaps are optional context for V4, not a prerequisite for comparing held-out performance. Adaptive-versus-adaptive comparisons alone do not test V4. No uncertainty estimates establish the significance of small differences.

versions.untested_parts: Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers.
Does not test the full range of adaptive optimizers or establish a training–test gap; results use task-specific recipes and do not report training performance.
Tests batch size with NovoGrad on ImageNet and speech recognition, not language models; does not compare all proposed recipe adaptations.
Dropout effects and removal of dropout with weight decay.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its relation to generalization gaps.
Removal of memorized training examples and resulting test accuracy.

rows.subject: ResNet-50v2
rows.operation_detail: Trained with SGD; reported single-crop ImageNet validation accuracy.
rows.note: No training accuracy is reported, so the training–test gap cannot be assessed.
rows.check: Valid SGD reference for R2–R3; its accuracy alone does not establish an adaptive-optimizer penalty. Missing training accuracy does not invalidate the held-out comparison.

rows.subject: ResNet-50v2
rows.operation_detail: Trained with AdamW; reported single-crop ImageNet validation accuracy.
rows.note: The authors describe this as the best accuracy achieved after extensive hyperparameter search.
rows.check: Against R1, AdamW is only 0.02 percentage points worse in top-1 accuracy. This is a very small penalty after extensive hyperparameter search, including weight decay; it is not a limited-tuning Adam comparison.

rows.subject: ResNet-50v2
rows.operation_detail: Trained with NovoGrad; reported single-crop ImageNet validation accuracy.
rows.note: Higher held-out accuracy than the SGD and AdamW rows, but training performance is not reported.
rows.check: Adaptive NovoGrad exceeds SGD by 0.56 percentage points top-1 accuracy. The comparison bears on adaptive optimization despite absent training accuracy, but uses different schedules and weight decay.

relationships.condition: ResNet-50v2 on ImageNet, 100 epochs, extensively tuned AdamW
relationships.reason: R1–R2 show nearly equal top-1 accuracy, 76.38% versus 76.36%, consistent with the qualification that broader tuning and decoupled decay can remove most of the penalty.
relationships.display_finding: AdamW achieved 76.36% top-1 accuracy versus SGD's 76.38%, without established run-to-run uncertainty.

relationships.reason: R1 and R3 show NovoGrad reaching 76.94% versus SGD's 76.38%; the adaptive-optimizer penalty depends on the optimizer and recipe.

relationships.condition: Speech-recognition extension: Jasper, Adam versus momentum SGD, 400 epochs
relationships.reason: R4–R5 show higher Adam WER on all four splits, including test-clean 5.27% versus 4.22%; the limited-tuning restriction remains unverified.
